title: The Crest Jewel: Viveka First
hookLine: a desperate seeker falls at a teacher's feet, and the book still puts his own clear sight first
carry: viveka: telling the real from the unreal
tomorrow: trust the guru completely, or only his good deeds?
last: THE QUESTIONS ARE PART OF THE BOW.

lines: FEAR NOT: THERE IS A WAY.
cards: In an old Sanskrit book, a young seeker comes to a teacher and falls at his feet. In paraphrase: I'm burning in the forest fire of birth and death. Save me.
A teacher could do a lot with a student that desperate. Ask for money. Ask for total obedience.
This one says, in paraphrase: fear not; there is a way across. And then he hands the student back something of his own. The book is the Vivekachudamani, the crest jewel of discernment.
Its title doesn't name the guru. It names the seeker's clear sight. Why would a book about being taught start there?

teach.h: VIVEKA: THE REAL FROM THE UNREAL.
teach.b: Tradition attributes the book to Shankara, though some scholars question that. Its word is viveka: telling the real from the unreal. The classic picture in Advaita: at dusk, a man sees a snake on the path and jumps back.
Someone brings a lamp. It was a coil of rope all along. Advaita reads our deepest fear that way.
We take what changes for what lasts, and take ourselves to be a body and a bundle of moods, when the self, the atman, is the rope under the snake.
Viveka is the lamp. Teachers say that's why it heads the book's list of what a seeker needs: then letting go of craving, then inner disciplines, then the longing to be free.
The book paints the teacher too: learned, free of desire, a knower of Brahman, calm like a fire that has burned through its fuel. Put the two pictures side by side and the puzzle solves itself.
A book that only said obey wouldn't need the student's sight at all. This one sends the student in with the lamp lit.

That isn't suspicion. Suspicion decides the worst before it looks. Viveka just looks: at the teacher, at the teaching, and first at the seeker's own wishes, the wish for a shortcut, the wish to hear only what feels good.

how: In Advaita Vedanta, the Vivekachudamani's list of what a seeker needs begins with viveka, discernment between the real and the unreal; its picture of the rope mistaken for a snake is one teachers of that tradition still use.

games.q: what does “modern gurus and their cautions” mean?
o: teachers today, weighed by what old texts ask of them
the fees gurus charge for their advanced lessons
a ban on following any guru born after the Vedas

games.q: the seeker and the teacher. tap the pairs.
p: telling the real from the unreal
a fire that has burned its fuel
the real, mistaken in the dark

s: the book's first requirement for a seeker is obedience
it's viveka, discernment, telling the real from the unreal.
viveka means assuming a teacher is a fraud
suspicion decides before it looks; viveka just looks clearly.
the book also paints the teacher, calm like a burned-out fire
learned, free of desire, a knower of Brahman, and calm.

games.q: a friend's new wellness coach says her doubts are just ego, and offers a costly next level. she asks what you think. what would viveka do?
o: trust the coach: doubts are what block progress.
look clearly: does the teaching hold up, and what does she want from it?
tell her it's a scam: anyone who charges is a fraud.
games.why: Viveka isn't obedience and it isn't suspicion. It looks clearly at the teacher, the teaching, and the seeker's own wishes.

practice: Advaita teachers practice viveka by sorting the seer from the seen. Notice one sound around you, then one feeling in the body, then one passing thought. Each one comes, and goes.
Quietly note each: seen. Then rest a moment as the one who notices, which hasn't come or gone. If that's too much today, just hear one sound plainly, and set down the story you add to it.

wordCard.voice: Modern gurus and their cautions. Today's caution: viveka, the lamp the seeker carries through the door.

orig.note: Sanskrit: viveka, discernment, the first requirement in the Vivekachudamani.

carryVoice: Something to keep: viveka, telling the real from the unreal, with the lamp lit even at the guru's door. See you tomorrow.

Vivekachudamani, verses on the seeker's qualifications (viveka listed first; then dispassion, the six disciplines, the longing for freedom)
